# Telegram (MTProto)

- Content-pack id today: `telegram` (`telegram.org`, `t.me`, `telegram.me`, `telesco.pe`)
- Status: names **PARTIAL** (no network allowlist read). MTProto framing **READY** as a **PROTOCOL** item: after the Go merge, Go only, vector-tested
- Sources accessed: 2026-11-18

## 1. What it is

Messaging. Telegram publishes its client-server transport protocol, MTProto, which makes a structural
profile possible without relying on names.

## 2. Transport and ports

"The TCP transport is implemented simply by sending the payloads generated by the chosen MTProto transport
over a plain TCP socket on ports 80, 443, 5222 or other" [S2]. WebSocket and HTTP(S) transports also exist;
"When using the WebSocket transport, transport obfuscation is required" [S2].

## 3. Observable evidence

Structure, from the primary specification [S1].

"The server recognizes these different protocols (and distinguishes them from HTTP, too) by the header" [S1]:

| Transport | Client's first bytes | Envelope |
|---|---|---|
| Abridged | single byte `0xef` | length/4 in 1 byte (< 127), or `0x7f` + 3-byte little-endian length/4; quick-ACK sets the top bit (`0xff` form) |
| Intermediate | int `0xeeeeeeee` | 4-byte little-endian length, then payload |
| Padded intermediate | int `0xdddddddd` | as intermediate, plus 0 to 15 random padding bytes |
| Full | no marker; first packet has sequence number 0 | `len` (4 bytes LE, includes itself), `seqno` (4 bytes, first packet 0), payload, `crc` (CRC32 over length, seqno and payload) |
| Obfuscated (any of the above) | 64 random bytes | random by design: the first int "must not be equal to" `0xdddddddd`, `0xeeeeeeee`, `POST`, `GET `, `HEAD `; bytes 4 to 8 must not be `0x00000000` |

The server "will not send" `0xef`, `0xeeeeeeee` or `0xdddddddd` as its first bytes [S1]. These are client-side markers.

## 4. Encrypted-traffic caveats

- **Obfuscated transport is designed to be unrecognisable** [S1]. It is mandatory for WebSocket [S2] and
  used through MTProxy, so a profile can only identify the non-obfuscated transports.
- Over a CONNECT proxy, a Telegram client using the TCP transport sends MTProto bytes directly. A client
  using WebSocket over HTTPS shows only TLS with SNI.

## 5. Confidence and false-positive risks

| Observable | Level | Limits |
|---|---|---|
| Full transport: `len` consistent with the segment, `seqno` = 0, valid CRC32 | **S**, strong | CRC32 over the first packet makes chance matches unlikely |
| Intermediate `0xeeeeeeee` + plausible length | **S**, medium | 4-byte marker; the length bound limits false positives |
| Padded intermediate `0xdddddddd` + plausible length | **S**, medium | as above |
| Abridged `0xef` + length byte | **S**, weak | One-byte marker. Needs at least the first envelope to be length-consistent, or it collides with arbitrary binary |
| Obfuscated | not identifiable | By design [S1] |
| Names (`telegram.org` and others) | **U** | No allowlist page read this batch |

## 6. Synthetic test vectors

For the Go profile.

| # | Input (client direction, first segment) | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | `ef` + `0x02` + 8 payload bytes | telegram (abridged) |
| P2 | `ef` + `7f 80 00 00` + 512 payload bytes | telegram (abridged, long form) |
| P3 | `ee ee ee ee` + `10 00 00 00` + 16 payload bytes | telegram (intermediate) |
| P4 | `dd dd dd dd` + `13 00 00 00` + 16 payload + 3 padding bytes | telegram (padded intermediate) |
| P5 | full: `len=12+N` (LE) + `00 00 00 00` + N payload bytes + correct CRC32 | telegram (full) |
| N1 | P5 with one CRC bit flipped | not telegram |
| N2 | P3 with a length larger than the configured budget | not identified (budget or malformed) |
| N3 | 64 random bytes whose first int is not a marker (obfuscated) | unknown, never telegram |
| N4 | `ef` followed by an inconsistent length | not telegram |
| N5 | every split point and single-byte chunking of P1 to P5 | same final observation (contract C1) |

## 7. Sources

- [S1] Telegram, "MTProto transports", `https://core.telegram.org/mtproto/mtproto-transports.md`, accessed 2026-11-18.
- [S2] Telegram, "Transport protocols", `https://core.telegram.org/mtproto/transports.md`, accessed 2026-11-18.

## 8. Catalog delta and recommendation

- PROTOCOL (later queue): a `telegram` (MTProto) TCP family for the abridged, intermediate, padded
  intermediate and full transports as in section 3, with full-transport CRC32 validation; no obfuscated
  claim. This is a new parser, so it is Go-only after the merge.
- Names: no change until a Telegram network allowlist is read.
